title: Assignment manifest
description: tests/<slug>/manifest.json. Declares only what the workflow has to know before grade.sh runs — which toolchains to install, whether student code gets a network, how long to allow. Everything else (services, fixtures, the test invocation itself) is grade.sh's business, because that is bash and needs no schema. Absent, the defaults here apply.

network.description: `none` runs student code in a network namespace with only loopback, and is the stronger sandbox. It is only usable when nothing in the assignment needs to reach the internet at grade time: no npm install, no image pull, no cargo fetch, and no `services`. Every assignment in this repo today needs `full` — learning-bitcoin-from-command-line has the student's own setup.sh download Bitcoin Core, which is the exercise. Dependencies for a `none` assignment must be vendored into the template or staged by prefetch.sh.

toolchains.description: Installed before grade.sh runs. Omit a key to skip it. The templates try to install nvm and rustup themselves at test time; doing it here instead is faster, cached, and works under `network: none`.

services.description: Whether grade.sh brings up containers. Only used to decide whether the workflow adds a teardown step; grade.sh starts them itself via services_up. Incompatible with `network: none` — the daemon runs outside the namespace, so published ports would be unreachable even if the images were already local.

timeoutMinutes.description: Overrides the assignment's configured timeout when this suite needs longer — a large image pull, a chain to sync. Omit to use what the backend dispatched.
